name: New York City Pre-K for All
executionNotes: Requires NYC child-capacity and maternal labor-force population builders; the later restricted-data estimate is an evaluation target, not a directly reproducible public-data outcome.
forecastQuestion: Before the first expansion year, how quickly would full-day pre-K enrollment scale and what later change in maternal labor-force participation would be consistent with the rollout?
summary: Forecast capacity, enrollment, and maternal labor-force response before the first expansion school year.

sources.title: Ready to Launch: NYC's Implementation Plan for Free, High-Quality, Full-Day Universal Pre-Kindergarten
sources.locator: Implementation timeline, enrollment targets, and provider-capacity plan

sources.title: NYC Social Indicators Report
sources.locator: Section 2, page 29: over 53,000 enrolled in year one and 68,500 by fall 2015

sources.title: Kids to School and Moms to Work
sources.locator: Abstract: triple-difference estimate of a 5 percentage-point increase

targets.label: Maternal labor-force participation effect
targets.notes: Triple-difference estimate, not a raw before-after change.

confounds: The expansion occurred in two phases.
Public ACS geography and preschool detail limit exact independent replication.
The maternal-employment estimate uses restricted Census data.
evaluationDesign: Administrative enrollment backtest plus a later triple-difference labor-force estimate.

verification.method: Every source URL was fetched and compared against the document it claims to be, and every scored figure was looked for in the source it cites.
findings: Every source resolved and every figure was found verbatim, with correct page numbers. Enrollment 53,000 and 68,500 are on page 29 of the NYC Social Indicators Report; the 5 percentage point maternal labour force effect is the abstract of Census working paper CES-25-62.
